name: Application
description: The Application object refers to the active Microsoft Access application.
remarks: The Application object contains all Access objects and collections. Use the Application object to apply methods or property settings to the entire Access application. For example, you can use the SetOption method of the Application object to set database options from Visual Basic. The following example shows how you can set the Display Status Bar check box on the Current Database tab of the Access Options dialog box. Access is a COM component that supports Automation, formerly called OLE Automation. You can manipulate Access objects from another application that also supports Automation. To do this, you use the Application object. For example, Microsoft Visual Basic is a COM component. You can open an Access database from Visual Basic and work with its objects.

properties.name: Application
properties.description: Use the Application property to access the active Microsoft Access Application object and its related properties. Read-only Application object.

properties.name: Parent
properties.description: Returns the parent object for the specified object. Read-only.

properties.name: CodeContextObject
properties.description: Use the CodeContextObject property to determine the object in which a macro or Visual Basic code is executing. Read-only Object.

properties.name: MenuBar
properties.description: Specifies a custom menu to display for a Microsoft Access database. Read/write String.

properties.name: CurrentObjectType
properties.description: Use the CurrentObjectType property together with the Application object to determine the type of the active database object (table, query, form, report, macro, module, server view, database diagram, or stored procedure). The active database object is the object that has the focus or in which code is running. Read-only AcObjectType.

properties.name: CurrentObjectName
properties.description: Use the CurrentObjectName property with the Application object to determine the name of the active database object. The active database object is the object that has the focus or in which code is running. Read-only String.

properties.name: Forms
properties.description: Use the Forms property to return a read-only reference to the Forms collection and its related properties.

properties.name: Reports
properties.description: Use the Reports property to access the read-only Reports collection and its related properties.

properties.name: Screen

properties.name: DoCmd
properties.description: Use the DoCmd property to access the read-only DoCmd object and its related methods. Read-only DoCmd.

properties.name: ShortcutMenuBar

properties.name: Visible

properties.name: UserControl

properties.name: IsCompiled

properties.name: CodeData

properties.name: Name

properties.name: LanguageSettings

properties.name: FileDialog

methods.name: GetOption
methods.signature: GetOption(OptionName As String) As Variant
methods.description: The GetOption method returns the current value of an option in the Access Options dialog box, available by choosing the Microsoft Office button, and then choosing Access Options. Variant.

parameters.name: OptionName
parameters.description: The name of the option. For a list of option name argument strings, see Set options from Visual Basic.

methods.name: SetOption
methods.signature: SetOption(OptionName As String, Setting As Variant)
methods.description: The SetOption method sets the current value of an option in the Access Options dialog box.

parameters.name: OptionName
parameters.description: The name of the option. For a list of option name argument strings, see Set options from Visual Basic.

parameters.name: Setting
parameters.description: A value corresponding to the option setting. The value of the setting argument depends on the possible settings for a particular option.

methods.name: Echo
methods.signature: Echo(EchoOn As Integer, [bstrStatusBarText As String])
methods.description: The Echo method specifies whether Microsoft Access repaints the display screen.

parameters.name: EchoOn
parameters.description: True (default) indicates that the screen is repainted.

parameters.name: bstrStatusBarText
parameters.description: A string expression that specifies the text to display in the status bar when repainting is turned on or off.

methods.name: CloseCurrentDatabase
methods.signature: CloseCurrentDatabase()
methods.description: Use the CloseCurrentDatabase method to close the current database, either a Microsoft Access database or an Access project (.adp) from another application that has opened a database through Automation.

methods.name: Quit
methods.signature: Quit([Option As AcQuitOption])
methods.description: The Quit method quits Microsoft Access. You can select one of several options for saving a database object before quitting.

methods.name: SysCmd
methods.signature: SysCmd(Action As AcSysCmdAction, [Argument2 As Variant], [Argument3 As Variant]) As Variant
methods.description: Use the SysCmd method to display a progress meter or optional specified text in the status bar, return information about Microsoft Access and its associated files, or return the state of a specified database object (to indicate whether the object is open, is a new object, or has been changed but not saved). Variant.

parameters.name: Action
parameters.description: An AcSysCmdAction constant that identifies the type of action to take. This set of constants applies to a progress meter. The SysCmd method returns a Null if these actions are successful. Otherwise, Access generates a run-time error.

parameters.name: Argument2
parameters.description: The text to be displayed left-aligned in the status bar. This argument is required when the Action argument is acSysCmdInitMeter, acSysCmdUpdateMeter, or acSysCmdSetStatus; this argument isn't valid for other Action argument values. NOTE: When you specify the acSysCmdGetObjectState value for the Action parameter, you must specify the appropriate AcObjectType constant.

parameters.name: Argument3
parameters.description: A numeric expression that controls the display of the progress meter. This argument is required when the Action argument is acSysCmdInitMeter; this argument isn't valid for other Action argument values. NOTE: When you specify the acSysCmdGetObjectState value for the Action parameter, you must specify the name of the database object.

methods.name: CreateForm
methods.signature: CreateForm([Database As Variant], [FormTemplate As Variant]) As Form
methods.description: The CreateForm method creates a form and returns a Form object.

parameters.name: Database

methods.name: CreateReport

methods.description: The CreateReport method creates a report and returns a Report object. For example, suppose you are building a custom wizard to create a sales report. Use the CreateReport method in your wizard to create a new report based on a specified report template.

parameters.name: ReportTemplate
parameters.description: The name of the report that you want to use as a template to create a new report.

methods.name: CreateGroupLevel
methods.signature: CreateGroupLevel(ReportName As String, Expression As String, Header As Integer, Footer As Integer) As Long
methods.description: Use the CreateGroupLevel method to specify a field or expression on which to group or sort data in a report.

parameters.name: ReportName
parameters.description: The name of the report that will contain the new group level.

parameters.name: Expression
parameters.description: The field or expression to sort or group on.

parameters.name: Header
parameters.description: Indicates that a field or expression will have an associated group header. If the Header argument is True (1), the field or expression will have a group header. If the Header argument is False (0), the field or expression won't. You can create a header by setting the argument to True.

parameters.name: Footer
parameters.description: Indicates a field or expression will have an associated group footer. If the Footer argument is True (1), the field or expression will have a group footer. If the Footer argument is False (0), the field or expression won't. You can create a footer by setting the argument to True.

methods.name: DMin
methods.signature: DMin(Expr As String, Domain As String, [Criteria As Variant]) As Variant
methods.description: Use the DMin function to determine the minimum value in a specified set of records (a domain).

parameters.name: Expr
parameters.description: An expression that identifies the field for which you want to find the minimum or maximum value. It can be a string expression identifying a field in a table or query, or it can be an expression that performs calculation on data in that field. In expr, you can include the name of a field in a table, a control on a form, a constant, or a function. If expr includes a function, it can be either built-in or user-defined, but not another domain aggregate or SQL aggregate function.

parameters.name: Domain
parameters.description: A string expression identifying the set of records that constitutes the domain. It can be a table name or a query name for a query that does not require a parameter.

parameters.name: Criteria
parameters.description: An optional string expression used to restrict the range of data on which the DMin function is performed. For example, criteria is often equivalent to the WHERE clause in an SQL expression, without the word WHERE. If criteria is omitted, the DMin function evaluates expr against the entire domain. Any field that is included in criteria must also be a field in domain; otherwise, the DMin function returns a Null.

methods.name: DDEInitiate
methods.signature: DDEInitiate(Application As String, Topic As String) As Variant
methods.description: Use the DDEInitiate function to begin a dynamic data exchange (DDE) conversation with another application. The DDEInitiate function opens a DDE channel for transfer of data between a DDE server and a client application.

parameters.name: Application
parameters.description: A string expression identifying an application that can participate in a DDE conversation. Usually, the application argument is the name of an .exe file (without the .exe extension) for a Microsoft Windows-based application, such as Microsoft Excel.

parameters.name: Topic
parameters.description: A string expression that is the name of a topic recognized by the application argument. Check the application's documentation for a list of topics.

methods.name: DDEExecute
methods.signature: DDEExecute(ChanNum As Variant, Command As String)
methods.description: Use the DDEExecute statement to send a command from a client application to a server application over an open dynamic data exchange (DDE) channel.

parameters.name: ChanNum
parameters.description: A channel number, the long integer returned by the DDEInitiate function.

parameters.name: Command
parameters.description: A command recognized by the server application. Check the server application's documentation for a list of these commands.

methods.name: DDEPoke
methods.signature: DDEPoke(ChanNum As Variant, Item As String, Data As String)
methods.description: Use the DDEPoke statement to supply text data from a client application to a server application over an open dynamic data exchange (DDE) channel.

parameters.name: ChanNum
parameters.description: A channel number, an integer returned by the DDEInitiate function.

parameters.name: Item
parameters.description: The name of a data item recognized by the application specified by the DDEInitiate function. Check the application's documentation for a list of possible items.

parameters.name: Data
parameters.description: The data to be supplied to the other application.

methods.name: DDERequest
methods.signature: DDERequest(ChanNum As Variant, Item As String) As String
methods.description: Use the DDERequest function over an open dynamic data exchange (DDE) channel to request an item of information from a DDE server application.

parameters.name: ChanNum

parameters.name: Address
parameters.description: A string expression that evaluates to a valid hyperlink address.

parameters.name: SubAddress
parameters.description: A string expression that evaluates to a named location in the document specified by the address argument. The default is a zero-length string (" ").

parameters.name: NewWindow
parameters.description: A Boolean value where True (1) opens the document in a new window and False (0) opens the document in the current window. The default is False.

parameters.name: AddHistory
parameters.description: A Boolean value where True adds the hyperlink to the History folder and False doesn't add the hyperlink to the History folder. The default is True.

parameters.name: ExtraInfo
parameters.description: A string or an array of Byte data that specifies additional information for navigating to a hyperlink. For example, this argument may be used to specify a search parameter for an .asp or .idc file. In your web browser, the extrainfo argument may appear after the hyperlink address, separated from the address by a question mark (?). You don't need to include the question mark when you specify the extrainfo argument.

parameters.name: Method
parameters.description: An MsoExtraInfoMethod constant that specifies how the extrainfo argument is attached.

parameters.name: HeaderInfo

methods.name: EuroConvert
methods.signature: EuroConvert(Number As Double, SourceCurrency As String, TargetCurrency As String, [FullPrecision As Variant], [TriangulationPrecision As Variant]) As Double
methods.description: Use the EuroConvert function to convert a number to euro, or from euro to a participating currency. You can also use it to convert a number from one participating currency to another by using the euro as an intermediary (triangulation). The EuroConvert function uses fixed conversion rates established by the European Union.

parameters.name: Number
parameters.description: The number you want to convert, or a reference to a field containing the number.

parameters.name: SourceCurrency
parameters.description: A string expression, or reference to a field containing the string, corresponding to the International Standards Organization (ISO) acronym for the currency you want to convert. Can be one of the ISO codes listed in the Remarks section.

parameters.name: TargetCurrency
parameters.description: A string expression, or reference to a field containing the string, corresponding to the ISO code of the currency to which you want to convert the number. For a list of ISO codes, see the Remarks section.

parameters.name: FullPrecision
parameters.description: A Boolean value where True (1) ignores the currency-specific rounding rules (called display precision in the sourcecurrency argument description) and uses the 6-significant-digit conversion factor with no follow-up rounding. False (0) uses the currency-specific rounding rules to display the result. If the parameter is omitted, the default value is False.

parameters.name: TriangulationPrecision
parameters.description: An Integer value greater than or equal to 3 that specifies the number of significant digits in the calculation precision used for the intermediate euro value when converting between two national/regional currencies.

parameters.name: OutputTarget
parameters.description: The file name and path for the resulting XML data file after applying the XSL file.

parameters.name: WellFormedXMLOutput

methods.description: The ExportXML method allows developers to export XML data, schemas, and presentation information from Microsoft SQL Server 2000 Desktop Engine (MSDE 2000), Microsoft SQL Server 6.5 or later, or the Microsoft Access database engine.

parameters.name: ObjectType
parameters.description: An AcExportXMLObjectType that represents the type of AccessObject object to export.

parameters.name: DataSource
parameters.description: The name of the AccessObject object to export. The default is the currently open object of the type specified by the ObjectType argument.

parameters.name: DataTarget
parameters.description: The file name and path for the exported data. If this argument is omitted, data is not exported.

parameters.name: SchemaTarget
parameters.description: The file name and path for the exported schema information. If this argument is omitted, schema information is not exported to a separate XML file.

parameters.name: PresentationTarget
parameters.description: The file name and path for the exported presentation information. If this argument is omitted, presentation information is not exported.

parameters.name: ImageTarget
parameters.description: The path for exported images. If this argument is omitted, images are not exported.

parameters.name: Encoding
parameters.description: An AcExportXMLEncoding constant that specifies the text encoding to use for the exported XML. The default value is acUTF8.

parameters.name: OtherFlags
parameters.description: A bit mask that specifies other behaviors associated with exporting to XML. Can be a combination of AcExportXMLOtherFlags constants.

parameters.name: WhereCondition
parameters.description: Specifies a subset of records to be exported.

parameters.name: AdditionalData
parameters.description: Specifies additional tables to export. This argument is ignored if the OtherFlags argument is set to acLiveReportSource.
